authored.summary: The rate of change of a triple-smoothed log price, filtering out short swings, with a signal line and zero crosses
authored.description:
## What it shows
A line in its own pane: the natural log of the close is smoothed by three exponential averages in a row, each over **Length** bars (18 by default), and TRIX is the one-bar change of the result times 10,000 — the smoothed rate of change in hundredths of a percent. A dashed zero line runs through the middle. With **Show signal line** on (the default), a **Signal** line averages TRIX over **Signal length** bars (9 by default).

## How to read it
- Above zero, the smoothed trend is rising; below zero, it is falling.
- The triple smoothing removes most short swings, so a zero cross marks a change in the underlying trend rather than a single bar's noise.
- A cross of the signal line is an earlier, less filtered turn.
- Alerts are available for **Crossed above zero**, **Crossed below zero**, **Crossed above signal** and **Crossed below signal**; the signal alerts work even while the signal line is hidden.

## Limits
- The heavy smoothing makes it slow: it confirms turns well after price has made them.
- Nothing is drawn until three full **Length** windows have passed (52 bars with the default), and the signal line starts **Signal length** − 1 bars after that.
